title: Creating Transient Cell Membrane Pores Using a Standard Inkjet Printer
protocol: Using pliers or an adjustable wrench, grasp the green top of the cartridge and twist back and forth several times until it breaks free.
Use screwdrivers to pry off the clear plastic piece now exposed.
Empty any remaining material from the reservoir.
Remove the plastic protective tape covering the printer contacts and print head.
Flush the reservoirs with water using a pipette or syringe.
Submerge the cartridge in de-ionized water and sonicate for 15 minutes before printing.
Submerge the cartridge in de-ionized water and sonicate for 15 minutes after printing.
Spray 70% ethanol into the cartridge to create an aseptic environment.
Culture 3T3 fibroblasts on T-75 flasks at approximately 1.3x10^4 cells/cm² in DMEM with 10% FBS.
Incubate the culture for two days at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Make a fluorescent g-actin stock solution at a concentration of 50 μg/ml in PBS.
Passage the cultured 3T3 fibroblasts.
Remove the media from the flask and rinse twice with PBS.
Cover cells with 5 ml of 0.25% Trypsin+EDTA and incubate for 5 minutes.
Add 5 ml of fresh medium to the cell suspension and transfer it into a 15 ml conical centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 1000 rpm for 5 minutes.
Aspirate the spent medium from the centrifuged cells.
Resuspend the cells in PBS with fluorescent g-actin stock solution to create bioink with a final concentration of g-actin of 10 μg/ml and a cell concentration of 1x10^5 cells/ml.
Power on the bioprinter and allow it to warm up.
Place the desired printing surface (22 mm x 22 mm coverslips) on the center of the stage prepared in step 1.
Create a printing pattern file using Microsoft Word or any other drawing software.
Load the prepared cartridge with desired cell suspension.
Pipette approximately 100-120 μl of cell suspension into the small circular well at the bottom of the cartridge compartment.
Print the file using the HP Deskjet 500 Printer.
For best results, print smaller patterns multiple times (5) by changing the number of copies in the word processing program.
Pull up on the paper feed mechanism wire when the cartridge moves to the "ready position".
Release the paper feed mechanism after every printed page for multiple copies.
Raise the paper feed mechanism wire again after releasing it for each page.
The printer will print onto the coverslip placed on the center of the printing stage.
Create a continuous line pattern across the majority of the microscope slide using Microsoft Word.
Print bioink and cells in a straight line on the substrate.
Note an increase in background fluorescence immediately after printing due to free excess fluorescent actin monomers in the bioink solution.
Add growth media to wash away excess monomer from the substrate, reducing background fluorescence over time.
Observe 3T3 fibroblasts 3 hours post-printing using a modified inkjet printer; cells show incorporated fluorescently tagged actin monomers.
Capture microscopy images of 3T3 fibroblasts printed in a localized printing zone at 20x magnification.
